name: Books
description: Read EPUB and PDF books and listen to audiobooks that already live on your NAS. Folders are browsed through the EthOS file API, so nothing is copied and your permissions still apply; titles, narrators, descriptions, covers and your place in every title are kept per account, and missing metadata is filled from Apple Books, Google Books and Open Library.
author: SyncHot
changelog: 2.0.2: a refresh no longer renames an established title or author because a provider offered a near-miss edition (Basia. Wielka księga pytań for Basia Wielka ksiega) — different editions still fill the description, genres and cover, and a candidate picked by hand is always applied. 2.0.1: a metadata refresh repairs libraries scanned by 1.5.0 — titles and authors that were taken from release folder names are re-parsed from the path (and narrators/series/years recovered) before the lookup, so Cięcie, Konfrontacja, Blade Runner, Wojna or Osiem milionów dróg do szczęścia match without a rescan. Polish ł now folds like l, so Łukasz Pilip and Paweł are recognised as names; the cover is taken from the best candidate that actually has artwork, and the stored query no longer contains bitrate/release noise. 2.0.0: metadata and covers done properly. Folder names and audio tags are parsed offline (Author - Title, Cykl … Tom …, release names, narrator after czyta, ID3/MP4/FLAC/OGG title+artist+album+track, Calibre .opf sidecars), so an author is never a release folder name again. Missing data comes from a provider chain — Apple Books (Poland) first, then Google Books (optional key) and Open Library — and fills title, author, narrator, series, year, publisher, ISBN, pages, genres, rating and a description. A Metadata & cover panel lists ranked candidates, allows a manual cover or its removal, and a generated poster covers whatever the providers miss. Library records migrate to schema 2; manual fields, provider metadata and covers survive rescans. 1.5.0: missing metadata and covers can now be filled from Open Library — a Fetch metadata button in the library, plus an option to do it automatically after a scan; matching prefers the correct title (Author - Title names), never overwrites manual edits, retries unmatched titles after 30 days, and downloads covers through the package service (no browser CORS limits). 1.4.0: covers are picked up from the folder during a scan — cover.jpg, folder.jpg, front.jpg, okladka.* or an image named after the book file or folder; embedded EPUB/audio art still wins, and a PDF folder cover replaces the rendered first page. 1.3.0: download titles to your device — books from the card menu, reader bar or audiobooks table, and single audiobook tracks with a ⤓ button in the player; bytes stream through /api/files/download, so nothing is copied on the NAS. 1.2.1: shorter release notes in Package Center (no behaviour change). 1.2.0: audiobook tracks carry their duration and embedded cover art, reading positions from several devices merge by newest write, and the library answers ETag/304. 1.1.0: shared folders and individual titles from other accounts — a “Shared with me” section in Folders & Scan and the library, read-only scanning and playback, and a Share button on your own scan folders (requires EthOS 2.13.3). 1.0.0: first release — a library for EPUB, PDF and audiobooks with per-account progress. Add one or more folders, scan them through the EthOS file API (no copying, no extra share access), and read in a paginated or scrolled reader with light, sepia and dark themes. Audiobooks play from .m4b files or folders of .mp3/.flac tracks with resume, speed, skip and a sleep timer. Covers, titles, authors and series are extracted in the browser; the package service stores metadata only.
